Sampled ranking measures candidate-dependent performance; it does not reliably estimate full-catalog ranking or preserve model ordering. [Krichene and Rendle](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/) establish this inconsistency; [RecSys 2025 research](https://doi.org/10.1145/3705328.3748086) distinguishes sampling fidelity, discriminative resolution, exposure robustness and alignment with ground truth. [A 2024 sequential-recommendation study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.17276) compares random, popularity, in-batch and adaptive training negatives. Training-negative design and evaluation-candidate design must therefore be documented separately; a larger training margin alone cannot establish generalization.

Suggested diagnostic framework, inferred from these findings: use fixed training-only prefixes with the next interaction excluded from the input; repeat evaluation across seeded uniform, popularity-weighted and popularity-matched unique candidate pools, plus full-catalog ranking where affordable. Report HR@10, positive rank, candidate counts and variation across draws, stratified by training-derived target popularity and history length. Prefix targets already used during fitting provide retrospective fit diagnostics, not independent generalization evidence. Keep the host’s 99-negative validation protocol unchanged and use its four-category macro HR@10 for selection; auxiliary probes cannot substitute for that result.

Validate probe sensitivity with paired history shuffling, truncation and unrelated-history replacement, holding targets and candidates fixed. Changes indicate sensitivity, not automatically beneficial sequence modeling. When user IDs exist, bootstrap users within categories, retain all prefixes for each sampled user, and pair resamples across conditions; report intervals for differences and category-macro averages. Candidate-draw variation and training-seed uncertainty are separate. Return undefined measurements as null with reasons: unavailable user IDs, empty strata, constant-valued correlations, absent full-catalog evaluation or unmeasured validation agreement. Unobserved exposure propensities and simulator traits cannot support causal debiasing claims.
